themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints surged to 34 THIS WEEK compared to a 7.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 346% spike (z-score: 7.87)—suggesting a sudden, acute noise problem affecting residential quality of life in East Harlem this week.
evidence: 34 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.6 weekly average (346% spike, z-score: 7.87)
Statistically significant deviation indicating acute, recent emergence rather than chronic issue
Aligns with community board history requesting traffic enforcement agents—suggests longstanding enforcement gaps now manifesting acutely
reporting_angles: Street-level reporting: identify where vehicle noise is worst (specific blocks, times of day); interview affected residents and businesses
NYPD enforcement angle: are noise enforcement units responding? Why the sudden spike—new construction, event, changed traffic patterns?

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Explode
themes_detail.summary: Park rules violations jumped to 4 complaints THIS WEEK from a historical baseline of 0.1 per week—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—signaling either new problematic activity in district parks or a rapid change in enforcement/reporting this week.
evidence: 4 park rules violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% spike, z-score: 11.72)
Highest z-score spike in dataset—statistically extreme deviation
Mirrors spike in 'Litter Basket Request' complaints (also THIS WEEK at 3 complaints vs. 0.1 avg, +2300%), suggesting park degradation/overuse
reporting_angles: Which parks are affected? Visit Marcus Garvey Park, East River Waterfront Park, Thomas Jefferson Park to observe current conditions
NYC Parks reporting: what violations are being reported? New enforcement crackdown, or genuine increase in rule-breaking behavior?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge Continues
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints reached 16 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 967% from the 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 9.17), representing a sustained, severe uptick in unhoused populations or visible street homelessness in East Harlem over the past two weeks.
evidence: 16 encampment complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 1.5 weekly average (967% spike, z-score: 9.17)
Concurrent spike in 'Dead Animal' complaints (3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 avg, +1100%) suggests broader sanitation/public health crisis in encampment areas
Concurrent spike in 'Non-Emergency Police Matter' complaints (16 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.2 avg, +205%) suggests safety concerns alongside encampments
reporting_angles: Street mapping: where are encampments concentrated? Document locations, sizes, services available or lacking (sanitation, mental health resources)
Services reporting: interview HRA, outreach teams; are there adequate shelter beds? Why the sudden surge now?

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK from a 0.4 weekly baseline—a 700% increase (z-score: 3.77)—suggesting a potential food safety incident or outbreak affecting multiple residents in East Harlem.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 3.77)
Cluster pattern within one week suggests common source rather than coincidental illnesses
Aligns with community board history requesting 'programs to address public health issues'
reporting_angles: DOHMH investigation: has the Health Department identified a source? Is there an active restaurant or vendor investigation?
Ground reporting: interview affected residents about symptoms, timeline, and establishment involved; check if complaints mention same restaurant

themes_detail.label: Vegetation Overgrowth
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints reached 3 LAST WEEK from a 0.1 weekly average—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—indicating acute tree maintenance failures affecting sidewalk safety and sight lines across East Harlem.
evidence: 3 overgrown tree/branch complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Mirrors 'Litter Basket Request' spike THIS WEEK, suggesting broader park/streetscape maintenance failure
Aligns with community board budget requests for 'park, building, or access improvements'
reporting_angles: Visual documentation: photograph overgrown trees and branches blocking sidewalks; map locations of complaints
NYC Parks/Sanitation accountability: why delayed maintenance? Is there a backlog of tree trimming requests?
